conversations.title: Woman With Dwarfism Opens Up About Dating, and the Behavior She Can’t Ignore
conversations.reply: A woman with dwarfism drawing a hard line between curiosity and actual interest. Disabled daters keep naming this exact split: being approached like a novelty is not the same as being wanted, and the two get confused constantly on first dates.

conversations.title: Parkinson’s drastically changed how they have sex. They're not alone.
conversations.reply: A neurologist stating plainly what most GP appointments skip past: Parkinson's changes sex, and almost nobody raises it before diagnosis lands. Disabled people have been naming that exact silence for far longer than this headline suggests.

conversations.title: Time to Pay Attention: This Is Bigger Than Any One Policy
conversations.reply: Rights rolled back one quiet amendment at a time is not a policy footnote, it is exactly what disabled communities have described for years: protection only holds while somebody is still willing to fight for it.

conversations.title: People in Jersey asked to share their views on island life
conversations.reply: Jersey asking residents to describe island life is the easy part. The real test lands after the survey closes: whether anyone acts on what disabled islanders actually flag, rather than filing it beside last year's consultation.

conversations.title: Aurora proclamation of Disability Pride Month seen as part of efforts to better support residents with disabilities
conversations.reply: A mayor reading out a Disability Pride Month proclamation costs nothing. Aurora's disabled residents will judge the month by whether one inaccessible building or event actually changes, not by which words got read at the podium.

conversations.title: Leeds Pride 2026 Set to Draw 60,000 as City Marks 20 Years of Celebration
conversations.reply: Sixty thousand people at Leeds Pride after twenty years is a real milestone. For disabled attendees the sharper measure is step-free routes in, accessible toilets, and viewing areas that do not disappear the moment the crowd thickens.

target: Shani Dhanda (UK disability activist and broadcaster)
target_reply: Shani Dhanda has spent years naming the exact gap this account tracks daily: venues that call themselves accessible until someone actually tries the door, and daters who disappear the moment disability stops being theoretical. That kind of clarity is worth amplifying, not softening.

instagram_hitlist.who: A disabled dating creator who posts about matches disappearing after they disclose a condition or share a mobility aid photo
instagram_hitlist.why: Direct alignment with the disclosure-and-vanish pattern disabled daters describe again and again
instagram_hitlist.comment: That moment right after disclosure, when replies slow down then stop, comes up in disabled dater accounts far too often to be coincidence. Naming it like this matters more than most people realise.

instagram_hitlist.who: #accessibility, searching for a fresh access-fail post about a venue with steps, no ramp or a lift permanently out of order
instagram_hitlist.why: Direct match with the venue-exclusion pattern that needs naming, not filing away
instagram_hitlist.comment: A broken lift or a flight of steps at the only entrance is not bad luck, it is a decision someone made and never revisited. Buildings get changed all the time when the will is there.

instagram_hitlist.who: An interabled couple account posting about everyday life together, including how they navigate dates or social plans
instagram_hitlist.why: Living counter-evidence to the assumption that disabled people are undateable, worth backing publicly
instagram_hitlist.comment: This is what gets left out of every headline asking whether people would date a disabled partner. Real relationships, documented in public, answer that question better than any survey.

instagram_hitlist.who: #wheelchairlife, looking for a post about a night out ruined by steps, no accessible toilet or a venue with zero step-free route
instagram_hitlist.why: Matches the nightlife exclusion theme directly, especially where a scene brands itself as fun for everyone
instagram_hitlist.comment: A venue that markets itself as the place to be but has no way in for a wheelchair user is not an oversight, it is a choice nobody wants to put their name to. Manchester's nightlife has run on this shrug for years.

instagram_hitlist.who: A Manchester-based access campaigner or disability advocate posting about a specific bar, club or Pride event and its step-free access
instagram_hitlist.why: Local and specific, useful for the Manchester angle and the Pride/nightlife exclusion pattern
instagram_hitlist.comment: An event calling itself inclusive while the entrance has steps is describing itself, not the experience of anyone using a wheelchair. Worth saying loudly rather than letting it pass as normal.

instagram_hitlist.who: #disabilitydating, searching for a post venting about being matched then ghosted the moment a condition comes up mid-conversation
instagram_hitlist.why: Core evidence for the central position: disclosure triggers disappearance, not honesty
instagram_hitlist.comment: Same story again, warm messages right up until disclosure, then radio silence dressed up as busyness. Disabled daters have been describing this exact sequence for years and it is never framed as the actual issue.

x_candidates.author: haleymossart
x_candidates.post: Haley Moss on X: "I’m really proud of this piece I got to write about #disability and dating while disabled, and I’m eternally grateful for the wonderful folks with different conditions and diagnoses who shared their stories with me for @GQ
x_candidates.reply: Good. Every honest account of dating while disabled chips away at the fiction that most daters are upfront about who they'll actually stay for. More writing like this, not less.

x_candidates.author: stevenspohn
x_candidates.post: Steven Spohn (Spawn) on X: "There is a hidden "disability tax" on dating that nobody wants to talk about. From the physical toll to the literal cost of accessibility, dating while disabled is expensive. I mean, dating is hard, and long-dist
x_candidates.reply: The cost of just getting to a date, the accessible transport, the extra planning time, never makes it into anyone's idea of what dating should cost. Calling it a tax is generous; it's a toll nobody chose to charge.

x_candidates.author: 6WConsulting
x_candidates.post: Dating with a disability can be frustrating. I am pleased to ... ## Post. Dating with a disability can be frustrating. I am pleased to recommend @DateabilityApp, created by sisters Alexa and Jacqueline Child. Web: ow.ly/6sJS50P0HSp App Stor
x_candidates.reply: Recommending a dedicated app for disabled daters shouldn't be necessary, but the mainstream platforms made sure it is. Good that options exist.

x_candidates.author: KBMM
x_candidates.post: Karyn Miller-Medzon on X: "#Disabled people often marginalized, taunted on #DatingApps. A new #app aims 2 change that. #JacquelineChilds #AlexaChilds talk 2 @hereanowrobin about creating #inclusive #safe space 4 pple w/ disabilities & #chro
x_candidates.reply: Marginalised and taunted on mainstream dating apps isn't a glitch, it's the account disabled daters have given for years. Any app built to change that starts from an honest place the big platforms never bothered reaching.

x_candidates.author: KamiSIUMAN
x_candidates.post: Hello! We are looking for a wheelchair accessible venue ... Hello! We are looking for a wheelchair accessible venue (seamless access from entrance to exit) for a workshop in December, Klang Valley.
x_candidates.reply: Wanting seamless access from entrance to exit shouldn't take this much hunting, in Klang Valley or anywhere else. Genuinely, good luck finding it.

x_candidates.author: TransformBandH
x_candidates.post: Speakers Corner has a new home at the @Brunswickpub! Speakers Corner has a new home at the @Brunswickpub! ✨ - where we'll be using their wheelchair accessible venue
x_candidates.reply: A wheelchair accessible home for Speakers Corner is exactly the standard every venue should be judged against, not the exception worth a mention.

x_candidates.author: joewellscomic
x_candidates.post: All venues are wheelchair accessible and there are some ... All venues are wheelchair accessible and there are some additional accessibility things on the event listing.
x_candidates.reply: Listing accessibility details alongside the venue address is the bare minimum done properly. More events should treat it as basic information, not an afterthought.

x_candidates.author: WfPSolidCollect
x_candidates.post: ▶️ The Garifuna leaders will share the urgent situation ... The event is open to the public. There will be Spanish-English interpretation & the venue is wheelchair accessible. 0.
x_candidates.reply: Interpretation and wheelchair access both sorted for the same event is what genuine inclusion looks like, not a bonus feature bolted on afterwards.

x_candidates.author: GiveUsTheNight
x_candidates.post: Give Us The Night on X: "A survey has been launched by @DeptCultureIRL to gauge the experience of nightlife for those with disabilities in Ireland. We want the night to be more welcoming + accessible to all, and hope this will help to devel
x_candidates.reply: Ireland's nightlife has run on inaccessible venues for years while calling itself vibrant; a survey is overdue, and the real test is whether the policy that follows actually changes who can get in.
